text:
marta: Quick proposal: add a per-route "redaction_mode" + "consent_mode" toggle to the request logger. Reason: some endpoints need full request capture for debugging, others must never persist raw user PII.

alex: +1 on per-route. Can we also add a sampling override that respects a Consent header? e.g. X-Redwood-Consent: explicit | implied | none. If explicit, keep full payload in ephemeral storage then drop.

priya: UX note: Console should make it obvious which routes are in "explicit" mode. Ops mistakes here are high-risk for customers. Maybe a red badge and a required justification field on enable.

jamie: Implementation detail: we should avoid storing full payload in primary telemetry DB. Suggest queue -> ephemeral S3 with TTL 24h when consent=explicit. Also mark traces with a redaction level enum: NONE/ATTRIB_HASH/REDACTED_STRUCT.

marta: agreed. Draft config sketch: 
```
logging:
  route_overrides:
    "/api/generate":
      redaction_mode: REDACTED_STRUCT
      sampling_rate: 0.01
      consent_handling: honor_header
    "/debug/internal":
      redaction_mode: NONE
      sampling_rate: 1.0
      consent_handling: require_explicit
```

nina: legal: requiring a justification and audit trail is necessary for enterprise customers. Any persistent raw captures must be auditable and have retention caps. Also need KMS-wrapped storage for ephemeral blobs.

alex: question: how do we detect PII in free-text? Should we rely on the model-based detector or regex heuristics? Model detectors are better but heavier and risk leak during detection step.

jamie: propose hybrid: light heuristics first (emails, ssn patterns), then model classifier run in sandboxed environment that never logs its inputs. The classifier returns a redaction map (offsets) rather than the raw text. That map can be applied before storing.

priya: Product ask: make Console show an example sanitized sample for each route so customers can verify the redaction. Could be behind a permission.

marta: ops question: how will sampling interact with dynamic routing (cheap model fallback)? If fallback occurs post-logging we might log partial outputs that don't match final user experience. Need to tie logging to final output version.

sre-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure log pipeline supports tagging by final_model_version and route_id, add fallback_event tag.

alex: privacy edge-case: embeddings. Even hashed tokens can be reversible for small corpora. For routes that generate embeddings, we should default to NO_PERSIST unless explicit consent is present.

nina: agreed, embeddings = high risk. Default NO_PERSIST for embedding endpoints in EEA customers unless contract says otherwise.

marta: actionable items: 1) implement route_overrides config + console badge + justification flow (pri). 2) prototype hybrid PII detector (jamie). 3) ephemeral storage TTL + KMS + audit logs (ops + nina). 4) default NO_PERSIST for embeddings with region-aware policy (alex).

priya: I'll own the Console UX tasks. Marta, can you make a tiny RFC with the config schema and safety knobs?

marta: yup, I'll write RFC and ping #eng-all for comments. Draft will include sample JSON, retention defaults, and examples of redaction_level effects.

ops-bot: reminder: feature flag 'pii-route-controls' is available in staging. Use it for testing. :gear:

alex: thanks — will run a privacy review once RFC is up.

jamie: i'll queue a small eval harness to measure false-positives on name/email detection. Won't log actual inputs during evals.

marta: awesome. if no objections, i'll start RFC tomorrow and tag @nina for legal sign-off.

priya: :thumbsup:

end.
